name: ExplainViz
tagline: Turns a block of text or a concept into an explanatory diagram or visual breakdown, generated by AI.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core loop here is text in, structured diagram out, and that is one of the most reliably one-shottable things an LLM does. You ask a model for Mermaid or SVG, you render it in the browser, you add an export button, you are done before dinner. The hard part is not generation, it is layout taste: making a 14-node graph readable, keeping labels from colliding, picking the right diagram type without being told. A personal build will produce diagrams that are correct and ugly, which is usually fine for your own notes and not fine for a client deck. No network, no shared corpus, no data you cannot regenerate, so nothing structural keeps you paying.
coreLoopDIY: Paste text or a question, an LLM picks a diagram type and emits Mermaid, the page renders it live and exports PNG or SVG.
requirements: An LLM API key (Anthropic or OpenAI) in .env
whatYouLose: Layout polish: hand-tuned spacing, theming, and diagram styles that actually look presentable
Smart diagram-type selection tuned on real usage rather than one prompt's guess
Hosted links you can share with someone who does not have your repo
Non-Mermaid visual forms: animated walkthroughs, custom illustration, rich infographic layouts
Someone else fixing it when the model emits syntactically broken diagram code
moatNotes: The defensible part is prompt engineering plus rendering taste, both of which degrade into commodity as base models get better at structured output.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because nobody wants to debug Mermaid syntax errors at 11pm before a presentation. A paid tool has already absorbed the thousand small failures: the model emitting a flowchart when a sequence diagram was obvious, labels overflowing nodes, arrows crossing in ways that make a clear idea look confused. If diagrams are part of how you get paid, the subscription buys output you can hand to a stranger without apologizing. If they are for your own notes, the DIY version is genuinely good enough.
notes: One of those categories where the model does the hard work and the product does the grooming.
prompt:
Build a local-only web app called "diagram-it" that turns pasted text into an explanatory diagram.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- mermaid (npm package) rendered client-side
- One server route handler that calls the Anthropic Messages API
- No database, no auth, no accounts, no analytics, no telemetry

Behavior:
1. Single page. Left pane: a large textarea for source text plus a dropdown for "auto, flowchart, sequence, mindmap, class, timeline, ER". Right pane: the rendered diagram.
2. On submit, POST the text and the chosen type to /api/diagram. The route asks Claude to return ONLY valid Mermaid source, no prose, no code fences. When type is "auto", the model also picks the diagram type and returns it in a JSON wrapper: { "type": string, "mermaid": string }.
3. Render the Mermaid on the client. If Mermaid throws a parse error, show the error, show the raw source in an editable code box, and offer a "fix it" button that sends the broken source plus the error message back to the model for one repair attempt. This retry loop is mandatory, not optional.
4. The code box is always editable and re-renders on change with a 400ms debounce. Hand-editing must always be possible.
5. Buttons: "Copy Mermaid", "Download SVG", "Download PNG" (render the SVG to a canvas at 2x scale for the PNG).
6. Keep the last 10 diagrams in localStorage with a simple list to reload them.

Explicitly out of scope: animation, user accounts, sharing links, PDF export, collaborative editing, image-based diagrams.

Put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env.local and read it only on the server. Commit a .env.example. Write a README with setup in under ten lines. Make the default Mermaid theme neutral with generous node padding so output is legible without tweaking.
